A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PERSE and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Matching retained content across the expanded appendix and renumbered displays supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original avatar reconstruction, interpolation, ablation, and portrait-animation experiments, plus a user study with 229 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a real-versus-synthetic video training experiment in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: Equation (11) adds a weighted VGG perceptual term to the previously stated L1-plus-SSIM reconstruction objective. The Gaussian avatar architecture, CLIP-conditioned latent representation, DiffMorpher supervision, and LoRA attribute-transfer framework remain.

E1.justification: Sections 4.2 and 5.1 and Table 4 replace the ears and eyes categories with earrings and headphones, retaining nine attribute categories. Appendix C.2 also introduces real-video versus self-driven synthetic-video training conditions for avatar reconstruction.

E2.justification: The avatar comparisons retain PEGASUS, Conditional INSTA, and Conditional SplattingAvatar. The portrait-animation comparison retains Moore-AnimateAnyone, MimicMotion, and MegActor-Sigma. The new real/synthetic comparison is a training-data control within PERSE.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1.2 changes the reported avatar training budget from 26 to 112 epochs, the Gaussian target from 180,000 to 130,000, and upsampling intervals from two to five epochs. Appendix C.2 adds a real/synthetic training comparison using VBench-derived metrics and held-out rendering evaluation. These materially revise the reported protocol, without establishing that retained benchmark tables were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2, Table 6, and Figure 12 test whether generated-video inconsistencies affect avatar reconstruction by comparing training on real and self-driven synthetic videos. The existing CLIP and interpolation-loss ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run variability, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new comparison also reports point estimates without additional uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and 5 retain their numerical results. New Table 6 reports real/synthetic subject consistency of 0.9761/0.9719 and avatar PSNR of 22.26/21.23, alongside SSIM, LPIPS, and imaging-quality scores. Expanded qualitative galleries add accessory edits and additional reference identities; these are added results, not demonstrated same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Equation (11) changes the mathematical definition of reconstruction loss by adding the weighted VGG term. The remaining deformation, interpolation, diffusion, and LoRA formulations are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain single-portrait personalized generative avatars, synthetic attribute-video generation, smooth disentangled editing through interpolation supervision, and LoRA-based attribute transfer. V2 emphasizes automation more prominently, but v1 already described the pipeline as fully automated.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly argues that the avatar pipeline accommodates temporal inconsistencies and that real/synthetic training produces negligible quality differences. V2 also removes v1's explicit discussion of inferior portrait-Champ naturalness relative to Moore-AnimateAnyone, although Table 5 retains the corresponding scores.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 revises training instructions and specifies covariance shrinkage of 0.75, opacity pruning below 0.5, and replacement radius 0.004. Figure 21 newly documents user-study instructions, including identity preservation. Section D replaces a future release promise with stated public availability of code and synthetic-dataset samples and supplies a repository address, substantially changing reproducibility and access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds the VBench reference to support the new consistency and imaging-quality evaluation. The existing related-work coverage and positioning relative to PEGASUS and other avatar methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract and introduction edits, clarifies automated mask generation, standardizes portrait-Champ terminology, and adds acknowledgments. A new Appendix C.2 shifts the former C.2 to C.3, while the overall narrative and section organization remain.

P2.justification: V2 revises Figures 1-3 and 6, updates the attribute examples, and substantially expands the appendix's visual material with the inconsistency comparison, additional identity and hair-editing galleries, and a user-study screenshot. The original interpolation gallery and notation table are retained as Figure 20 and Table 7.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful evidence about real-versus-synthetic training, broader qualitative examples, clearer diagrams and study instructions, and public-release information. These modestly strengthen support and reproducibility. The gains are limited by conflicting animation-routing descriptions in Section 4.2 versus Appendix A.3.3 and removal of the earlier naturalness caveat; the main numerical comparisons remain unchanged.
